title: GPU driver crash clustering + repro harness prototype
content:
Purpose
- Capture notes from recent on-call runs where we saw repeated driver crashes (nvidia.ko panics / oops) that cluster by stacktrace signature.
- Sketch a minimal repro harness and automated clustering pipeline to speed root-cause identification and reduce noisy paging.

Summary of incidents observed (last 6 weeks)
- Symptom: host kernel OOPS / panic after a device fault while training small batch jobs. Node auto-evicted; subsequent attach attempts hit nv_peer_mem timeouts.
- Frequency: ~1-3 incidents/week on mixed fleet (A100x2, H100x1 hybrid pods).
- Commonalities: immediate pre-failure shows PCIe link retrain messages, then NVLink channel flaps for a few seconds, then a GPU page-fault and driver stack unwinding.
- Observable stacktrace groupings: two prominent signatures (A: gpu_kill_work + mmu_fault_handler path, B: nvlink_layer_reset -> driver-irq path).

Quick on-call playbook (minimum steps to collect repro data)
- When alerted: do NOT immediately reboot if node still reachable. Collect artifacts first. Priority: dmesg, journalctl, syslog, /var/log/nvidia/*, driver core dumps.
- Commands to run (copy paste):
  - sudo journalctl -u kubelet -S "-15m" --no-pager > /tmp/kubelet-recent.log
  - sudo dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg-$(date +%s).log
  - sudo ls -l /var/log/nvidia || true; sudo tar -czf /tmp/nvidia-logs.tgz /var/log/nvidia || true
  - sudo /usr/local/bin/gpu-collect-support --bundle /tmp/gpubundle-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).tgz (this script collects pcisys, nvlink stats, nv-hostengine logs, and lsmod)
  - if driver core created (look for /var/crash or /var/lib/systemd/coredump): sudo coredumpctl info --no-pager > /tmp/coredump-info.log
- Upload those bundles to S3 under s3://redwood-sre/gpu-debug/$(hostname)/ and attach to SRE ticket.

Clustering approach we used in trial
- Extract stacktrace fingerprints from dmesg and coredumpctl using heuristics: (function names + top-6 frames). Normalize addresses.
- Group incidents by fingerprint and annotate with: chassis id, GPU serial, driver version, kernel version, recent firmware versions, and nvlink fabric topology.
- Initial run on last 60 incidents: groups A and B cover ~72% of driver crash alerts; remainder are a mix of MMU panics and thermal watchdogs.

Key observations from clustered groups
- Group A (mmu_fault dominated) often correlates with: older driver (525.x) + mixed model pairing (A100 + older 80GB variant) + host kernel 6.2.x.
- Group B (nvlink-reset dominated) shows strong temporal correlation with scheduled power c-states being enabled after recent BIOS updates; suspect PCIe retrain under heavy NVLink traffic.
- Several nodes show recurring ECC correctable error increase ~12–48 hours before a crash. ECC surge might be an early signal.

Prototype repro harness (sketch)
- Goals: create a repeatable failure in lab to reproduce stacktrace fingerprints A/B and collect deterministic logs. Must be non-destructive and safe for warranty.
- Components: workload runner (small transformer micro-batch), synthetic NVLink stress tool (nvlink-stress-lite), PCIe retrain injector (pci_retrain.py - toggles link training via sysfs), memory hammer (memtest-ng targeted to GPU BAR mappings).
- High-level recipe:
  1) Start workload runner with small seq_len=512, batch=4 repeatedly for N iterations.
  2) After warmup (5 mins) start nvlink-stress-lite at low frequency.
  3) After 2–5 mins toggle PCIe retrain via: echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/<gpu>/reset (use caution; test in lab node)
  4) Monitor dmesg for the fingerprint. Increase intensity until either ECC corrective counters increase or driver oops replicates.
- Notes: this is a prototype; real injection requires hardware lab reservation and coordination with platform-engineering to avoid false alarms.

Automation proposals (short-term)
- Add automated fingerprinting to our existing alert pipeline: when driver crash alert fires, gather fingerprint and auto-attach probable cluster label to PagerDuty notification. Reduces pager noise for known clusters.
- Correlate ECC correctable counter trends (prometheus metric: node_gpu_ecc_correctable_count) with crash clusters; create a predictive alert that flags nodes exceeding local baseline + X sigma.
- Build a small Lambda that ingests kernel oops messages and pipes top frames to a classification model (initially rules-based).

Open hypotheses (to prioritize experiments)
- H1: PCIe retrain under NVLink heavy traffic triggers a driver race that surfaces as mmu_fault in certain driver versions. Repro by triggering retrain while running NVLink traffic.
- H2: ECC correctable accumulation is weakening GPU DMA windows and eventually causes page faults under high-memory workloads. Repro with mem-hammer + monitoring of correctable counters.
- H3: Firmware mismatch between host BIOS and GPU microcode causes edge-case timeout during hotlink negotiation. Check firmware inventory and test rolling back BIOS where practical.

Planned experiments (owners and timeline)
- E1: Bench lab repro attempt with controlled pci retrain toggles (owner: Ethan Park) — 2029-04-22 to 2029-04-26.
- E2: Run ECC drift baseline capture for fleet segment (owner: Maya Gonzalez; infra support from Samir) — 2 weeks starting 2029-04-19.
- E3: Driver upgrade matrix test in staging to see if newer 535.x or 540.x eliminates cluster A behaviors (owner: Asha Patel) — kickoff 2029-04-25.

What to avoid during triage
- Avoid immediate power-cycle of suspect node until we've captured kernel logs and driver core; a reboot can clear transient evidence.
- Avoid mass reboots across a rack; instead isolate an affected host and cordon its k8s node.

Remediation suggestions (when cluster label known)
- If cluster A fingerprint: recommend bump to driver 535.x and schedule canary on similar hardware.
- If cluster B fingerprint: temporarily disable aggressive c-states or implement PCIe ASPM conservative mode via BIOS if supported, pending deeper root cause.
- If ECC drift signal present: quarantine node and schedule proactive scrub + extended memtest in maintenance window.

Notes to infra & platform-eng
- Need a safe, documented mechanism for programmatic PCIe retrain in lab without triggering hardware-level isolation policies. Current /sys toggles sometimes cause firmware watchdogs.
- Request: add GPU serial to crash alerts so SREs can correlate hardware batches quickly.

Next steps / action items (short list)
- [ ] Ethan: run E1 in hardware lab and report reproducer success/failure by 2029-04-26.
- [ ] Maya & Samir: start fleet ECC baseline capture and share dashboards by 2029-05-03.
- [ ] Asha: coordinate driver matrix test in staging; raise PR to sre-tools to add basic stacktrace fingerprint extraction.
- [ ] Platform-eng: confirm whether BIOS rollback images are available for suspect racks.

Appendix: useful commands and helpers
- gpu-collect-support (sre-tools): collects nvlink stats, pcisys info, /proc/interrupts, lsmod, gpu topology.
- small one-liners we found handy:
  - sudo grep -E "NVRM:.*GPU" /var/log/nvidia/* | tail -n 200
  - sudo journalctl -k --since "-30m" | grep -i -E "oops|panic|nvlink|nvrm|gpu"
  - python3 scripts/stack-fingerprint.py /tmp/dmesg.log > /tmp/fingerprint.txt

Choppy notes / unresolved
- We still don't know whether the driver bug is strictly timing-related or depends on a stateful corruption that accumulates (ECC hints it might).
- Need better mapping from chassis -> physical port mapping in our inventory (current mapping is sometimes stale).

If you want to push this to final: open a confluence page, paste cleaned repro steps, and link lab reservation. For now this is a scratchpad for SRE + platform experiments.

Slack threads referenced (for context): #sre-gpu-triage (pinned messages), #infra-bios-updates
